🔀 Multi-repo context Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf, Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts ## Linked repositories findings ### `Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf` - PurRDF’s OWL parser accepts qualified cardinality fillers via `owl:onDataRange` and routes them through the same expression path as `owl:onClass` (`crates/entail/src/owl_dl/parser.rs:988-1000`). The PR’s ontology changes from `logic:onClass logic:Thing` to `logic:onDataRange rdfs:Literal` are compatible with this parser contract. [::Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf::] - PurRDF’s datatype-range engine explicitly places `xsd:anyURI` in its unmodeled remainder, producing undecided results rather than native range proofs (`crates/xsd/src/range.rs` module documentation). Any new ontology-side `anyURI` reasoning must therefore remain implemented in the consuming reasoner rather than relying on PurRDF range entailment. [::Blackcat-Informatics/purrdf::] ### `Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts` - GTS compares literals by exact lexical form, datatype IRI, language, and direction; it does not apply datatype lexical canonicalization (`docs/GTS-SPEC.md:700-706`). The PR’s `anyURI` whitespace/facet semantics must not be expected to arise from GTS transport. [::Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts::] - Rust and Go GTS validators accept `xsd:anyURI` lexical forms unchanged (`rust/src/xsd.rs:114`, `go/xsd/xsd.go:106`), confirming that URI facet interpretation belongs to the reasoning layer. - Untyped literals are defaulted to `xsd:string` during GTS interning (`rust/src/rdf.rs:985-1002`), so removing language tags from the PR’s constraint-message literals does not alter their datatype during transport. [::Blackcat-Informatics/gmeow-gts::]
